lecture_summary: The lecture connects torque-based balance and center of mass to continuous mass distributions, then develops moment of inertia, rotational kinetic energy, direct rod integrations, the parallel-axis theorem, and additive inertia for composite objects.

videos.title: Center of Mass Physics Problems - Basic Introduction
videos.reason: Builds the mass-weighted-position and balance intuition needed before the lecture’s continuous center-of-mass calculations.

videos.title: Inertia - Basic Introduction, Torque, Angular Acceleration, Newton's Second Law, Rotational Motion
videos.reason: Provides the strongest conceptual treatment of rotational inertia, its dependence on mass distribution and axis choice, and its relationship to torque and angular acceleration.

videos.title: Parallel Axis Theorem & Moment of Inertia - Physics Practice Problems
videos.reason: Directly teaches the shifted-axis method used to obtain and verify the lecture’s end-axis and off-center rod results.

coverage_gaps: No strong playlist match covers the variable-density workflow dm = λ(x)dx, normalization of λ(x) = Cx from total mass, and integration yielding x_cm = 2L/3.
No listed video directly derives rod moments of inertia by integration, including I_cm = ML²/12, I_end = ML²/3, the variable-density result ML²/2, or the axis-at-L/3 result ML²/9.
No direct match covers adding the inertia of a rod and an attached point mass about a common axis.

The closest rotational-kinetic-energy video focuses on rolling bodies, inclines, and pulleys rather than this lecture’s derivation of K_rot = Iω²/2 and rod examples, so it was omitted from the minimal set.
